Pune Startup Froncort.AI Gets $2.3 Mn Google.org Grant For AI Disease Screening App
Froncort.AI, a Pune-based healthcare AI startup, has received a $2.3 million grant from Google.org to build a mobile tool that tells frontline health workers which households to screen first for tuberculosis and other infections.
The grant comes with $200,000 in Google Cloud credits and pro bono engineering support. It is Google.org’s second grant to the company, after funding a validation study of its AI-NETRA platform in 2025.
How the Company Was Selected
Froncort.AI is one of 15 organisations worldwide picked for the Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation, a $30 million programme whose recipients were announced on 15 September.
Read More: Sachin Tendulkar Backs Waste Management Startup Recykal
Funding Confido Health Raises $12.5 Million To Automate Healthcare Administration With AI Funding Prodoc AI Raises Seed Funding From Dr A. Velumani Family Office
Google.org said winners were chosen from more than 2,600 proposals. Froncort.AI is one of four recipients in the health category, alongside Flexbone, Helium Health Foundation and the University of Warwick.
Read More: How to Choose the Best Travel Agency in Jaipur for a Memorable Rajasthan Holiday
That ratio explains why the grant matters more than its size. Being selected from 2,600 applicants is third-party validation that a health ministry or a state programme can cite.
What mAI-NETRA Does
The grant funds mAI-NETRA, a mobile version of the company’s public health platform.
Froncort.AI’s system combines government health programme data with satellite-derived insights from Google’s Earth AI models. It also weighs local indicators such as settlement density, land use, rainfall and flood exposure.
From that, it flags higher-risk areas within 300-metre zones and turns them into ranked work plans, household clusters and routes that health workers can follow on field visits.
The Froncort.AI app works offline with automatic sync and offers multilingual voice guidance. Matters in districts where connectivity is patchy.
Why Routing Beats Testing Alone
India’s tuberculosis programme already has tests, drugs and reporting systems. What it lacks is a way to decide where to spend a health worker’s day.
Sending a worker street by street in a high-burden district is expensive and random. Sending the same worker to a ranked cluster of households with recent flooding and dense housing is a different use of the same salary.
Froncort.AI already has TB and malaria modules are already in place. The platform is being built to cover six diseases: TB, leprosy, malaria, dengue, cholera and leptospirosis.
What the Founder Says
“The world does not lack experts. It lacks their reach,” said Ujjwal Rao, founder and chief executive of Froncort.AI. He described AI-NETRA as putting that expertise in the health worker’s hands at the door, showing where to go, whom to screen and when.
India’s health system already collects enormous amounts of data through national programmes. The gap is turning that data into a route a health worker can follow on a Tuesday morning.

The transaction closed on November 1, 2026, and strengthens Focus's business management platform with additional expertise serving clients in television, film, and related creative industries.

articles.text:
Focus Financial Partners: Acquisition Of ML Management Partners Expands Entertainment Industry Business Management Services
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:53 AM
Focus Financial Partners: Acquisition Of ML Management Partners Expands Entertainment Industry Business Management Services
Focus Financial Partners, a financial services firm providing wealth management, family office, and business management services, has acquired ML Management Partners (MLM), a New York City-based business management firm specializing in serving entertainment industry professionals and high-net-worth individuals. The transaction closed on November 1, 2026, and strengthens Focus’s business management platform with additional expertise serving clients in television, film, and related creative industries.
Founded in 1988 by Mark Landesman, ML Management Partners provides business management and family office services to entertainment professionals, including actors, comedians, directors, producers, writers, industry executives, and other creative professionals.
The firm maintains offices in New York City and Los Angeles.
The acquisition expands Focus’s portfolio of specialized business management firms and provides MLM with access to additional resources and infrastructure.
Focus reported more than $550 billion in collectively advised assets as of June 30, 2026.
Expanding Focus’s Entertainment Industry Capabilities
The acquisition strengthens Focus Financial Partners’ presence in a specialized segment of the financial services industry.
Business management firms serving entertainment professionals often provide services tailored to clients with complex financial affairs and careers involving multiple income sources.
These clients may include performers, producers, directors, writers, and executives working across television, film, and other entertainment businesses.
ML Management Partners has developed its business around these relationships over nearly four decades.
The firm’s experience extends beyond traditional entertainment industry clients to include family office services for high-net-worth individuals.
Focus believes the acquisition supports its broader strategy of building a platform that combines specialized financial expertise with extensive operational resources.
The company has continued investing in businesses that complement its wealth management and family office services.
MLM adds an established client base and experienced leadership team to that platform.
ML Management Partners’ Nearly Four-Decade History
ML Management Partners was founded in 1988 by Mark Landesman.
The business initially focused primarily on serving comedians before expanding its services across the broader entertainment industry.
Today, MLM works with professionals both in front of and behind the camera, including talent, executives, producers, directors, and writers.
Its client base also includes individuals and businesses with specialized financial management requirements.
The firm operates from New York City with a second office in Los Angeles, providing a presence in two important centers of the U.S. entertainment industry.
Landesman has emphasized the importance of maintaining long-term relationships and personalized services for the firm’s clients.
He described the acquisition as an opportunity to preserve MLM’s established approach while accessing the broader resources of Focus.

articles.text:
Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Launches With Faster Agentic AI, 1 Million-Token Context Window, And New Multi-Model Orchestration
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 7:36 AM
Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Launches With Faster Agentic AI, 1 Million-Token Context Window, And New Multi-Model Orchestration
Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new artificial intelligence model designed to deliver faster execution, improved reasoning, and greater efficiency across software development, enterprise workflows, and everyday AI applications. The model features a 1 million-token context window, four adjustable reasoning levels, and expanded capabilities for autonomous AI agents, while Google is also introducing a multi-model orchestration system that coordinates different Gemini models within a single workflow.
Announced on November 12, 2026, Gemini 4 Hydrogen joins Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon models, which are designed for more demanding reasoning tasks.
While Carbon and Argon focus on complex problems requiring deeper analysis, Hydrogen emphasizes rapid execution across coding, research, data analysis, and other agentic workflows.
Google is making Hydrogen available across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and Google Antigravity for eligible paid subscribers.
The company has priced Hydrogen at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, with flat pricing across its entire 1 million-token context window.
Google says Hydrogen achieves a score of 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high reasoning setting, compared with 50 for Gemini 4 Argon. Hydrogen reaches 54 at its highest reasoning setting, known as xhigh.
New Orchestrator Coordinates Multiple Gemini Models
One of the most significant additions accompanying Hydrogen is Orchestrator, a new capability within Google Antigravity that dynamically switches between AI models during a single development session.
The technology is designed to use different models for different stages of a task rather than relying on one model throughout an entire workflow.
For example, Gemini 4 Carbon can handle complex architectural decisions or coordinate a development project, while Hydrogen performs code generation, testing, debugging, and verification.
Google says this approach allows developers to combine the reasoning capabilities of its frontier models with Hydrogen’s execution efficiency.
In Terminal-Bench 4.0 testing, Orchestrator achieved task success rates approaching those of Carbon while consuming an average of 24% less quota and completing tasks 19% faster.
The system also supports parallel AI agents operating across isolated workspaces.
These agents can work simultaneously on different parts of a software development project, potentially reducing execution time and resource consumption.
Google believes this multi-model approach can help organizations optimize AI workloads based on task complexity, latency requirements, and operating costs.
Major Improvements Over Gemini 3.8 Flash
Hydrogen represents a significant upgrade over Google’s previous Gemini 3.8 Flash model.
At its default high reasoning setting, Hydrogen completes tasks approximately 2.5 times faster while improving its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score from 18.2% to 57%, according to Google’s evaluations.
The company also reported that Hydrogen reduces fabricated claims by more than fivefold compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash.
